# dcbuilder.dev

> The public site of dcbuilder.eth. It covers research in Ethereum, programmable cryptography, digital identity, distributed systems and decentralized AI, alongside engineering, writing and angel investing.

The public Model Context Protocol (MCP) server is available at https://mcp.dcbuilder.dev/mcp over Streamable HTTP. Its tools are read-only and require no account, API key or OAuth credentials.

To connect Codex, run `codex mcp add dcbuilder_public --url https://mcp.dcbuilder.dev/mcp`. In another MCP client, add the same URL as a Streamable HTTP server. After connecting, use `tools/list` for the current tool schemas.

## Public pages

- [Home](https://dcbuilder.dev/): Research, engineering and angel investing interests.
- [About](https://dcbuilder.dev/about): Biography, roles and affiliations.
- [Blog](https://dcbuilder.dev/blog): Published articles. Append `/markdown` to an article URL for its plain Markdown version.
- [Portfolio](https://dcbuilder.dev/portfolio): Public angel investments, categories and hiring status.
- [News](https://dcbuilder.dev/news): Curated links, articles, announcements and portfolio updates.
- [Jobs](https://dcbuilder.dev/jobs): Public job listings and application links.
- [Candidates](https://dcbuilder.dev/candidates): Public candidate profiles, skills and availability.
- [Sitemap](https://dcbuilder.dev/sitemap.xml): Index of public site URLs.

## MCP tools

- `get_site_page` takes `page` (`home` or `about`) and returns the page content and its URL.
- `get_public_item` takes `collection` (`news`, `blog`, `candidates`, `portfolio` or `jobs`) and `id` from a search result. Use it to retrieve a single record or the full text of a published blog post.
- `search_news` supports `q`, `company`, `category`, `type`, `hidePortfolioUpdates`, `minRelevance`, `since` and `sort`.
- `search_blog` supports `q`, `source`, `minRelevance`, `since` and `sort`.
- `search_candidates` supports `q`, `location`, `availability`, `experience`, `tags` and `featured`. Anonymous profiles use a public alias.
- `search_portfolio` supports `q`, `category`, `categories`, `status`, `featured`, `hiring`, `main` and `sort`.
- `search_jobs` supports `q`, `company`, `type`, `role`, `location`, `remote`, `featured` and `tags`. Results include the original application link when available.

All search tools accept `limit` (default 20, maximum 50) and `offset` (default 0). Use `meta.hasMore` to tell whether another page is available. Dates in the `since` filter use `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Use the returned `url` to cite a result. For job applications, use `applyUrl` when present.
